title: SkillScreen: High-Recall Screening of Malicious Agent Skills with Decision Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.17727v2 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Agent skills turn natural-language instructions into actions, creating a security challenge: legitimate automation and malicious behaviour can look deceptively similar. A practical screen must catch nearly every attack while keeping the review load manageable. We present SkillScreen, a compact decision model trained to score skill maliciousness directly from SKILL$.$md in a single forward pass. On MaliciousSkillBench, SkillScreen flags 20-25% of benign skills at 99% recall on unseen attack families, substantially fewer than the word-level classifier and prompted LLM judges tested. Under the same training protocol, it also generalizes better than a fully fine-tuned encoder to unseen sources. Yet unfamiliar benign sources sharply increase false positives, showing that recognizing new attacks does not ensure reliable screening of new skill collections. Our results demonstrate the value of task-trained decision models for high-recall skill

translated_title: SkillScreen：基于决策模型的恶意智能体技能高召回率筛查
translated_abstract: 智能体技能将自然语言指令转化为具体操作，这带来了一项安全挑战：合法的自动化行为与恶意行为可能看起来惊人地相似。一个实用的筛查系统必须在几乎捕获每一次攻击的同时，保持审查负载可控。我们提出了 SkillScreen，这是一个紧凑的决策模型，经过训练可以直接从 SKILL.md 文件在单次前向传播中对技能的恶意程度进行评分。在 MaliciousSkillBench 基准上，SkillScreen 在对未见攻击族达到 99% 召回率的情况下，仅将 20-25% 的良性技能标记为可疑，明显少于所测试的词级分类器和提示式 LLM 判官。在相同的训练协议下，它对未见来源的泛化能力也优于全量微调的编码器。然而，陌生的良性来源会显著增加误报率，这表明能够识别新攻击并不等于能够可靠地筛查新的技能集合。我们的结果证明了针对特定任务训练的决策模型在高召回率技能筛查中的价值。
tldr: SkillScreen 是一个紧凑的决策模型，能在单次前向传播中直接对 SKILL.md 技能的恶意程度评分，在未见攻击族上达到 99% 召回率且误报远低于词级分类器和 LLM 判官，但对陌生良性来源的误报仍会显著上升。
en_tdlr: SkillScreen is a compact task-trained decision model that scores agent-skill maliciousness directly from SKILL.md in a single forward pass, achieving 99% recall on unseen attack families with far fewer false positives than word-level classifiers and prompted LLM judges, though unfamiliar benign sources still sharply increase false positives.
